edition.name: The mole people: life in the tunnels beneath New York City
edition.sourceProvenance: Frozen from the 1993 first-edition Open Library record, the Google Books work-family page, the Chicago Review Press product page, the CCLS Syndetics table of contents and professional reviews, later reporting recorded in manifests/source-ledger.json, and publisher-permitted listing excerpts used for narrow Chapter 1-5 support.

chapterBreakdown.gentle: Mac survives through harsh routine, naming, and discipline. The point is not spectacle. It is that scarcity has become organized enough to feel like a code.
chapterBreakdown.direct: Mac is read through method. Hunting rats, renaming them, and cooking them show survival becoming system rather than one desperate act.
chapterBreakdown.competitive: His code is built to beat hunger one day at a time, and the chapter refuses to call that code noble.

point.gentle: Mac turns survival into routine so scarcity does not fully own him.
point.direct: The portrait treats harsh method as dignity defense.
point.competitive: His code is survival discipline, not spectacle.

point.gentle: Naming helps make humiliation more manageable.
point.direct: Track rabbits shows language doing survival work.
point.competitive: The rename is pressure control, not cute irony.

point.gentle: The chapter keeps competence and damage together.
point.direct: Mac is neither a freak show nor a secret hero.
point.competitive: Respect the toughness without glamorizing the cage.

oneMinuteRecap.gentle: Mac survives through hard routine, but the chapter never lets that routine look clean or noble.
oneMinuteRecap.direct: Chapter 4 argues that competence under deprivation protects dignity while hardening into identity armor.
oneMinuteRecap.competitive: Mac wins small battles against hunger and may lose more of life to the siege.

chapterBreakdown.gentle: Mac enters through routine rather than confession. The lawful bundle gives an older man whose life is organized around hard competence, and that competence becomes the portrait spine.
chapterBreakdown.direct: Calling rats track rabbits matters because language helps Mac endure humiliation without denying reality. Naming is part of the survival mechanism, not a side detail.
chapterBreakdown.competitive: The Thoreau detail blocks lazy sorting. Mac cannot be reduced to grime, but the chapter also refuses to turn contrast into uplift.

point.direct: Method shows what scarcity has made necessary.
point.competitive: The code tells the story before biography does.

moreDetails.gentle: The chapter starts with practice because routine reveals pressure honestly.
moreDetails.direct: Method is the portrait spine because it shows deprivation answered with ritual.
moreDetails.competitive: Do not chase legend first. The code is already the dossier.

point.direct: Track rabbits is a survival phrase.
point.competitive: The rename is armor against humiliation.

moreDetails.gentle: Usable words can help a person stay intact during harsh necessity.
moreDetails.direct: The phrase creates psychological distance without denying what must be done.
moreDetails.competitive: Miss the naming move and you miss half the discipline.

point.direct: The quotation detail blocks crude sorting.
point.competitive: Culture enters to destroy lazy categories, not to rescue the scene.

moreDetails.gentle: Mac can be materially deprived and mentally companioned at the same time.
moreDetails.direct: Reflective life can remain active inside deprivation without cleansing it.
moreDetails.competitive: Keep the rats in frame or the portrait goes soft.

point.direct: Hard routine keeps Mac from total passivity before scarcity.
point.competitive: Action is how he resists humiliation.

moreDetails.gentle: Doing difficult things well can preserve a sense of self in a narrowed life.
moreDetails.direct: The chapter recognizes skill while refusing to call the condition free.
moreDetails.competitive: He is not powerless, but that does not mean he is winning.

point.gentle: Siege logic can become identity armor.
point.direct: What preserves the self can also trap the self in war mode.
point.competitive: The code that saves him may become the cage he cannot set down.

moreDetails.gentle: A survival routine can harden until letting go feels like losing the self it defended.
moreDetails.direct: This is the deeper contradiction: defensive competence carries cost once it becomes the only acceptable self-respect.
moreDetails.competitive: If war becomes the identity, peace starts to feel like exposure.

activationPrompt.direct: Identify one routine that looks impressive from outside but may actually be a defense against scarcity.
activationPrompt.competitive: Find one case where toughness earned respect while hiding the bad world that made toughness necessary.

oneMinuteRecap.gentle: Mac survives through method, language, and hard competence, but the chapter ties that competence to deprivation rather than heroism.
oneMinuteRecap.direct: The chapter teaches that naming, routine, and quotation all matter because survival here is practical and identity-forming.
oneMinuteRecap.competitive: Mac has edge, but the siege that forged it never stops charging interest.

chapterBreakdown.gentle: Mac's portrait is built from method because method shows what pressure has done to a life without pretending a full biography is available. Routine becomes moral posture as well as practical necessity.
chapterBreakdown.direct: Language is not decorative here. The rename reorganizes what survival feels like, which means Mac is managing meaning as well as hunger.
chapterBreakdown.competitive: The strongest reading rejects both gawking and cheap admiration. The chapter keeps dignity, scarcity, language, and cost live at the same time.

point.gentle: Method reveals pressure without a full biography.
point.direct: Routine is primary evidence of what scarcity has made necessary.

moreDetails.gentle: Repeated practice carries more truth than invented backstory could.
moreDetails.direct: Centering routine stays faithful to source limits while still making pressure visible.
moreDetails.competitive: You do not need a war memoir when the rituals already show the front line.

point.gentle: Naming changes what survival feels like.

point.gentle: Competence can be both dignity and confinement.
point.direct: Agency under siege preserves self-respect while narrowing self-respect.

moreDetails.gentle: Mac's routines prove he is not passive, but they also show how survival can become the dominant shape of life.
moreDetails.direct: This is the central contradiction: the code defeats humiliation locally while extending the war globally.

examples.title: Iris Decides Whether Hard Competence Is the Whole Story

scenario.gentle: Iris sees a client fixing a torn bag with perfect speed while a dented thermos rolls under the chair. She has to decide whether to praise the toughness or ask what pressure made it necessary.
scenario.direct: A caseworker sees impressive self-sufficiency in a harsh setting and must decide whether to celebrate the skill or investigate the scarcity behind it.
scenario.competitive: Iris can admire the edge and miss the wound, or read the edge as evidence of the war still running.

whatToDo.gentle: Respect the competence, but ask what deprivation the routine may be defending against.
whatToDo.direct: Treat the skill as real while refusing to confuse adaptation with a healthy environment.
whatToDo.competitive: Do not hand out medals for survival code before you name the siege.

whyItMatters.gentle: People often build impressive routines because their margin is gone.
whyItMatters.direct: The chapter teaches that competence can hide the pressure that produced it.
whyItMatters.competitive: If you glorify the armor, you strengthen the war.

examples.title: Mateo Reviews a Student Who Mistook Toughness for Stability

scenario.gentle: In a vocational workshop lit by a humming fluorescent strip, Mateo realizes he praised a student's grit all semester without noticing the student was living out of a car.
scenario.direct: An advisor reviews a case and sees that what looked like mature discipline was partly emergency adaptation.
scenario.competitive: Mateo confused siege performance for stable character and now has to ask what his praise concealed.

whatToDo.gentle: Re-read the behavior with the pressure context included and adjust support accordingly.
whatToDo.direct: Separate genuine capability from the deprivation that made the capability necessary.
whatToDo.competitive: Stop rewarding war mode as if it were ordinary thriving.

whyItMatters.gentle: Harsh competence can win respect while hiding cost.
whyItMatters.direct: The chapter warns against mistaking emergency discipline for proof that conditions are manageable.
whyItMatters.competitive: If institutions love toughness too much, they become collaborators with the pressure.

examples.title: June Learns Why Pride Can Sound Hard

scenario.gentle: June talks with her uncle at a kitchen table where work gloves still smell of oil. He speaks proudly about getting by on almost nothing.
scenario.direct: A family conversation reveals pride built around surviving with very little. The challenge is respecting the pride without romanticizing the scarcity.
scenario.competitive: June must resist two traps at once: pity that insults him and admiration that excuses the bad situation.

whatToDo.gentle: Acknowledge the skill and pride, then keep the conversation tied to cost.
whatToDo.direct: Honor self-respect without turning endurance into a lifestyle ideal.
whatToDo.competitive: Respect the fighter, not the battlefield.

whyItMatters.gentle: People may defend dignity through hardness when softer identities feel unsafe.
whyItMatters.direct: Mac's chapter helps explain why some forms of pride are built inside deprivation.
whyItMatters.competitive: If you call the war noble, you make exit feel like betrayal.

examples.title: Evan Predicts the Hidden Cost of a Perfect Routine

scenario.gentle: Evan keeps noticing that one employee never misses a task and keeps a grease-marked notebook. The reveal is that the routine is covering unstable housing.
scenario.direct: A manager sees flawless execution and later learns it is built on constant scarcity management outside work.
scenario.competitive: The strongest performer on the board is running siege logistics off the clock.

whatToDo.gentle: Read the routine as a clue and create room for support before the system crashes.
whatToDo.direct: Do not assume high performance means low pressure; ask what hidden conditions are feeding the rigidity.
whatToDo.competitive: Perfect discipline can be an alarm, not a victory lap.

whyItMatters.gentle: Hard routines often grow where people cannot afford mistakes.
whyItMatters.direct: The portrait teaches that methodical performance may be identity armor under pressure.
whyItMatters.competitive: If you only reward the code, you help weld it shut.

examples.title: Leila Chooses Whether to Praise Toughness or Name Scarcity

scenario.gentle: Leila is writing an advising note while a bus-transfer stub falls out of a folder. The student frames every setback as a test of toughness.
scenario.direct: An advisor has to decide if praising resilience will help or if it will hide the material pressure shaping the case.
scenario.competitive: Leila can endorse the armor or tell the truth about why the armor exists.

whatToDo.gentle: Document the pressure clearly and avoid language that turns hardship into character training.
whatToDo.direct: Name the scarcity, then support capability without glamorizing emergency.
whatToDo.competitive: Do not let toughness become paperwork that launders deprivation.

whyItMatters.gentle: Institutions often flatten hardship into grit when precision would be more honest.
whyItMatters.direct: The chapter warns that respect becomes distortion once it stops naming conditions.
whyItMatters.competitive: If you praise the war and omit the siege, you are not helping.

examples.title: Grant Reframes What He Thought Strength Meant

scenario.gentle: Before, Grant thought strength meant never needing anything. After watching a friend improvise dinner in an apartment with cracked tile by the sink and almost no food, he sees the skill differently.
scenario.direct: A friend's severe self-reliance stops looking admirable in the abstract once the scarcity behind it becomes visible.
scenario.competitive: Grant learns that what he called strength was partly a life cornered into precision.

whatToDo.gentle: Keep the respect, but attach it to the person rather than to the deprivation.
whatToDo.direct: Revise your definition of strength so it includes cost, not just execution.
whatToDo.competitive: Stop worshipping the armor and start seeing the pressure that forged it.

whyItMatters.gentle: The chapter changes how hard competence should be read in ordinary life.
whyItMatters.direct: Mac's portrait teaches that disciplined survival deserves clarity, not romance.
whyItMatters.competitive: A better reading keeps the edge visible without calling the cage freedom.

coreSkill.gentle: The core skill is learning to read harsh competence as both dignity and evidence of pressure.
coreSkill.direct: The core skill is disciplined interpretation: seeing routine, naming, and pride without glamorizing scarcity.
coreSkill.competitive: The edge is refusing to mistake war skill for a healthy life.

plan.gentle: If someone shows extreme self-sufficiency, then ask what pressure may have made that precision necessary.
plan.direct: If a routine looks unusually hardened, then investigate scarcity before rewarding it as pure excellence.
plan.competitive: If the code is flawless, check whether siege conditions built it.

plan.gentle: If a student is praised mainly for grit, then document the material pressure around the grit as well.
plan.direct: If resilience language is taking over the case, then name the deprivation that resilience is organizing around.
plan.competitive: If the institution loves toughness, force it to see the war feeding that toughness.

plan.gentle: If a loved one takes pride in getting by on very little, then respect the pride while staying honest about cost.
plan.direct: If survival pride appears, then avoid both pity and romantic admiration.
plan.competitive: If the armor speaks first, do not bow to it or mock it. Read the siege.

twentyFourHourChallenge.gentle: In the next day, notice one hard routine and ask whether it signals healthy stability or survival pressure.
twentyFourHourChallenge.direct: Within 24 hours, pick one admired competence and identify the hidden condition that may be producing it.
twentyFourHourChallenge.competitive: Before tomorrow ends, catch yourself praising toughness and ask what war you may be overlooking.

weeklyPractice.gentle: Once this week, practice describing someone's capability together with the cost it may be carrying.
weeklyPractice.direct: Weekly practice: when you see rigid self-sufficiency, add a pressure question before drawing a character conclusion.
weeklyPractice.competitive: Each week, refuse one opportunity to glamorize armor.

keyTakeawayCard.gentle: Mac survives by turning scarcity into hard routine, but the chapter never lets that routine become noble mythology.
keyTakeawayCard.direct: Chapter 4 teaches that competence under deprivation protects dignity while hardening into siege identity.
keyTakeawayCard.competitive: If you admire the code without naming the cage, you misread the whole war.
